findings.title: Second `downsize` definition silently overrides the existing 5-argument `downsize`
findings.body: `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` is defined after `def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` in the same class. Ruby has no overloading, so the later definition replaces the earlier one and the `max_width, max_height` version (lines 145-147) is dead code. Any existing caller using `downsize(from, to, width, height[, opts])` now binds `height` to `opts`. `optimize` then evaluates `opts[:allow_animation]` on an Integer or String, which raises TypeError, or it drops the real options. Fix by using a single method that accepts the dimensions string, and update or remove the old callers.

findings.title: Percentage geometry is passed to the animated GIF path, and the downsize result is never checked
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(..., "80%", allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails)` can route to `downsize_instructions_animated`. That delegates to `resize_instructions_animated`, which runs `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`. `--resize-fit` expects `WxH`, not a percentage, so gifsicle fails. The return value of `downsize` is ignored, so the loop retries the same failing command up to 5 times, and the oversized GIF is then rejected later by `Upload.create_for`. When animation is not allowed, the `[0]` frame selection silently drops the animation. The loop should stop on a `false` return, and the animated path should use a valid scale option such as `--scale`.

findings.title: Client-side size limit hard-coded to 10MB, ignoring site settings for images and attachments
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` used to come from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`. It is now a constant 10MB for every type, including `attachment`. Sites that configure `max_attachment_size_kb` below or above 10MB no longer get a correct client-side check. Smaller limits give no early rejection, so the file is uploaded and only then fails on the server. Larger limits are blocked client-side. The error dialog also reports 10240 KB, which can differ from the real limit. The 413 handler at line 246 has the same hard-coded value. Only the image case needed relaxing, to allow server-side downsizing. The attachment setting should still be honoured, and the magic number should be defined in one place.

findings.title: Changed `optimize`/`downsize` signatures and the new automatic downsizing have no tests
findings.body: The `optimize` signature changes from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`, and `dimensions` is removed. A new overload `downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts)` is added. `UploadsController#create_upload` also gains a retry loop that rewrites the uploaded temp file in place. No specs cover any of this. That includes images over and under `max_image_size_kb`, the 5-attempt cap, failure of the convert step, and animated GIFs. A spec would have caught the duplicate `downsize` definition.
